Chapter 6: The Courage to Challenge Assumptions.
Sometimes, the most powerful questions are the ones that make us just a little uncomfortable. They poke at the stories we've always believed, and nudge us to look at the rules we've followed without a second thought.
Have you ever caught yourself wondering, What if things aren’t really as they seem? It’s not easy to ask that—especially when everyone else around you seems perfectly happy with how things are.
Imagine a small-town librarian. She’s always stuck to the same routine—shelving books in the same old way, recommending the same familiar classics. Then, one day, a visitor walks in and asks, “Why are these books organized like this?” That simple question lingers. Suddenly, the librarian starts to see things differently: maybe the way things have always been done doesn’t actually help everyone. Some voices are hidden away on the bottom shelves, and some are missing altogether. Quietly, she begins to shift things around—bringing fresh stories to the front. At first, it’s subtle. But soon, more people are finding books that truly speak to them.
Most of us don’t realize just how many of our beliefs are inherited—passed down from our families, our culture, or just habits we never thought to question. It’s so easy to accept things as just the way they are. But every now and then, someone pauses and thinks, “Is this really true?”
That moment of doubt can feel pretty unsettling, like standing on shaky ground. But it’s right there, in that uneasy space, where real growth happens.
Take a young engineer, working at a company where everyone’s proud of their “tried and true” methods. She starts to quietly question why certain processes never seem to change. At first, her coworkers brush it off—“That’s just how we do things.” But she keeps asking, gently looking for evidence, suggesting little experiments. Slowly but surely, the team realizes that a few of those old habits are actually holding them back. By daring to challenge the way things have always been done, they unlock smarter, better ways to work together.
Now, challenging assumptions doesn’t mean you have to throw out every tradition. Sometimes, it’s about understanding the reasons behind those traditions—deciding what still fits, and what might be ready for a change. Think about a family revisiting their old rituals—holiday meals, bedtime stories—and asking, “What do these actually mean to us now?” The answers might lead to new traditions, or even a deeper appreciation for the ones you want to keep.
It’s so easy to drift through life on autopilot, just following the scripts that others have written for us. But those who are brave enough to stop, to question—even if it feels awkward or risky—find that the world opens up in unexpected ways. They become a little more flexible, more creative, and a whole lot more compassionate—toward themselves, and toward others.
The courage to challenge assumptions isn’t about rebelling for the sake of it. It’s about being honest. It’s about searching for the truth, even if it’s inconvenient. It’s about making room for new possibilities, for voices that haven’t been heard, for stories waiting to be told.
In the end, it’s a quiet kind of bravery—the willingness to ask, What if? and to follow wherever that question leads.
